label: The review mode's documents never reference the shared layer while its scripts pin two shared files, so the route carries two authorities for surface identity with no declared fork: rg over sk-code-review (excluding benchmark and changelog) hits only check-rule-copies.js:64,82 and its test, while SKILL.md, references/ and assets/ contain none; the hub claims detection lives once in shared/ (SKILL.md:135) and the review mode implements detect_surface_evidence itself. Either the mode consumes the shared detection contract or the packet declares the fork. Reproducing case: rg -n 'shared/references' over the mode's SKILL.md, references and assets exits 1. NEW P2.

Strengthening proposals for the review logic, ranked by proof value: (a) give check-review-findings.js a second pattern for the heading shape so both documented shapes are graded; (b) route the review mode's surface detection through the shared contract or derive its marker list from stack-detection.md section 2; (c) add the Obsidian token to the output contract and detection once (b) lands; (d) build a review-output contract fixture that feeds both checkers the documented good and bad shapes; (e) extend the canary's exact-string set with the AGENTS.md-level review floors it does not pin. NEW P2 proposal set; each item is cheap and independently testable.

Verified as deliberate: the hub keeps mode contracts packet-local (SKILL.md:137) and the review canary pins load-bearing wording in the shared standard and workflow-verify rather than copying it (check-rule-copies.js:64,82), which is the right shape of coupling. ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action; recorded so the zero-reference sweep in f-iter011-001 is not mistaken for a missing contract.
